findings.name: Property Tax Relief Claim for Seniors and Disabled Veterans (K-40SVR)
findings.description: Kansas provides an annual property tax refund to disabled veterans (50%+ permanent service-connected VA disability rating), seniors (65+), and qualifying surviving spouses via Form K-40SVR. Applicants must be Kansas residents for the entire claim year, must have owned and occupied a Kansas home during that year with an appraised value of $350,000 or less in the base year, and must have household income of $58,041 or less (2025 figures; Social Security benefits are excluded from Kansas adjusted gross income for this calculation). The refund equals the difference between the homestead's base-year property tax amount and the current-year property tax amount. Claims are filed annually with the Kansas Department of Revenue (Kansas WebFile or by mail) between January 1 and April 15, along with Federal Form 1040 pages 1-2 and a current VA disability rating letter; processing takes 20-24 weeks.
findings.value: Refund equal to the increase in homestead property tax over a base year
otherReqs: Kansas residency for the entire claim year
Household income $58,041 or less (2025 figure, adjusted annually)
Home appraised value $350,000 or less in base year
Owned and occupied the Kansas home during the claim year
Annual filing required, January 1 - April 15 deadline
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming 50%+ permanent service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: To be eligible a Veteran must be a Kansas resident, honorably discharged, and have a 50% or more permanent service-connected disability rating from the VA. You must have household income of $58,041 or less for 2025, own and occupy a home in Kansas during 2025, and your house cannot be valued at more than $350,000 in the base year. The refund will be the difference between the claimant's homestead property tax amount for a base year and the claimant's homestead property tax amount for the current year.

findings.name: Disabled Veterans License Plate
findings.description: Kansas issues a Disabled Veterans license plate at no registration fee (vehicle property/ad valorem tax still applies) to Kansas residents who served in the U.S. armed forces with a service-connected disability of at least 50%, or who qualify for compensation due to loss or permanent loss of use of one or both feet or hands, or permanent impairment of both eyes, or who are responsible for transporting a qualifying disabled veteran. The vehicle (auto, motorcycle, or truck registered for 20,000 lbs or less) must be titled in the applicant's name in Kansas or the applicant listed as lessee. Applicants submit Form TR-103 in person at the county treasurer's motor vehicle office, with certification signatures from the regional VA director and, if requesting the wheelchair symbol, a medical professional. Additional plates carry standard registration fees and property taxes.
findings.value: No registration fee for the first plate (vehicle property tax still applies)
otherReqs: Service-connected disability of 50%+, or qualifying loss/permanent loss of use of feet/hands, or permanent visual impairment, or responsible for transporting a qualifying disabled veteran
Vehicle titled in applicant's name in Kansas (or applicant listed as lessee)
Certification required from regional VA director; medical professional signature if requesting wheelchair symbol
Proof of valid insurance required at application
findings.agency: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles
documentation: Form TR-103 with VA regional director certification
findings.sourceExcerpt: To qualify, applicants must be a Kansas resident who served in the U.S. armed forces with a service-connected disability of at least 50% according to the laws administered by the veterans administration, OR qualify for compensation due to loss/permanent loss of use of feet, hands, or permanent visual impairment. Initial plate: no registration fee; property tax still applies.

findings.name: Disabled Veterans Hunting & Fishing License
findings.description: The Kansas Legislature annually appropriates funding for the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks to issue free annual hunting, fishing, or hunt/fish combination licenses to honorably-discharged Kansas resident veterans with certified service-related disabilities of 30% or more. Availability depends on annual funding, and applicants must reapply each year with current disabled-veteran entitlement papers proving at least 30% disability, along with a current Kansas driver's license or ID showing residency (and a Hunter's Education Card if applying for hunting and born on or after July 1, 1957).
findings.value: Free annual hunting, fishing, or hunt/fish combination license (subject to annual legislative funding)
otherReqs: Honorable discharge
Certified service-related disability of 30% or more
Must reapply annually
Current Kansas driver's license or ID required
Hunter's Education Card required for hunting if born on/after July 1, 1957
Subject to annual legislative appropriation/funding availability
findings.agency: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks
findings.form: Kansas Disabled Veterans Hunting & Fishing License Application
documentation: Current disabled veterans entitlement papers showing proof of 30%+ disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: Any Kansas resident who is an honorably-discharged military veteran with certified service-related disabilities of 30 percent or more qualifies and must apply each year for the annual licenses. Free hunting and fishing licenses are made available and issued based on funding, with applicants required to provide a copy of current disabled veterans entitlement papers showing proof of at least 30% disability.

findings.name: State/Local Government Employment Veterans' Preference
findings.description: Kansas gives honorably discharged veterans preference in initial employment and first promotion within city, county, and state government, provided the veteran is competent for the position; preference also extends to spouses of veterans with a 100% disability rating and to surviving spouses of veterans killed in action. Certain positions are excluded from preference, including elected offices, at-will positions, and roles requiring a physician or law license. Veterans and qualifying spouses eligible for preference are guaranteed an interview and consideration for the position, but preference does not guarantee a job offer; eligible veterans also receive consideration for promotional opportunities and higher retention standing during a workforce reduction.
findings.value: Preference in initial employment and first promotion within city, county, and state government; guaranteed interview and consideration
otherReqs: Honorable discharge required
Applicant must be competent for the position
Spouse preference limited to spouses of 100% disabled veterans or surviving spouses of those killed in action
Excludes elected offices, at-will positions, and physician/law-license positions
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge
VA documentation of 100% disability rating (for spouse preference)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Honorably discharged veterans are preferred in initial employment and first promotion within city, county, and state government if 'competent.' This preference also extends to spouses of 100% disabled veterans and surviving spouses of those killed in action. The preference excludes certain positions like elected offices, at-will roles, and those requiring physician or law licensure.

findings.name: Veteran Resident Tuition Rate
findings.description: Kansas law entitles a veteran, spouse, or dependent to pay Kansas public postsecondary institution tuition and fees at the resident rate, regardless of how long the dependent has resided in the state, if the service member was stationed in Kansas for at least 11 months during active service, or had established Kansas residency prior to active service, and was discharged or released under honorable or general-under-honorable-conditions discharge. Separately, under the federal Veterans Choice Act, veterans using Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits who live in Kansas (where their institution is located) and file a letter of intent to establish residency qualify for in-state tuition, as do their eligible spouses and dependent children. All current members of the armed forces (all branches, plus Kansas Army/Air National Guard and reserves) and their spouses/dependent children are also deemed Kansas residents for tuition purposes at Kansas public postsecondary institutions. Veterans confirm eligibility through the Office of the Registrar at their intended institution.
findings.value: Kansas resident tuition rate instead of nonresident tuition
otherReqs: Service member stationed in Kansas 11+ months during active service, or established KS residency before active service
Honorable or general-under-honorable-conditions discharge
Alternative path: using Post-9/11 GI Bill and living in Kansas with a filed letter of intent to establish residency
documentation: DD-214 or proof of qualifying discharge
Proof of Kansas stationing or residency
VA Certificate of Eligibility (for Post-9/11 GI Bill path)
findings.sourceExcerpt: A Veteran, spouse, or dependent is entitled to pay tuition and fees at an institution of higher education at the rates provided for Kansas residents without regard to the length of time the dependent has resided in the state if the service member was stationed in Kansas for at least 11 months during active service in the Armed Forces or had established residency in Kansas prior to active service, and was discharged under an honorable discharge or a general discharge under honorable conditions.

findings.name: Kansas Soldiers' Home (Fort Dodge) & Kansas Veterans' Home (Winfield)
findings.description: Kansas operates two state veterans homes: the Kansas Soldiers' Home in Fort Dodge (serving since 1890, ~5 miles east of Dodge City) and the Kansas Veterans' Home in Winfield. Preference for admission goes to wartime veterans with an honorable discharge; peacetime veterans, spouses, surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents may be admitted on a space-available basis, with priority given based on severity of medical care required. There are no income or net-worth eligibility limits, though applicants must disclose income/net worth for determining charges based on ability to pay; no veteran is denied admission for lack of income or excessive income. Required application documents include the Application for Admission, an Authorization to Receive & Release Protected Health Information, VA Form 10-5345 and VA Form 10-10EZ (veterans only), an immunization record, and DD-214 or equivalent proof of honorable discharge.
findings.value: Residential and skilled nursing care, with charges based on ability to pay
otherReqs: Honorable discharge (preference to wartime veterans); peacetime veterans/spouses/surviving spouses/Gold Star parents admitted space-available
No income/net-worth eligibility cap, but financial disclosure required to determine charges
DD-214, VA Form 10-5345, VA Form 10-10EZ, and immunization record required for veteran applicants
findings.form: Application for Admission; VA Form 10-5345; VA Form 10-10EZ
documentation: DD-214 or Military Honorable Discharge & Enlistment Record, or VA verification
findings.sourceExcerpt: Preference for admission is given to War-time veterans who have been Honorably Discharged. Peace-time Veterans, spouses, surviving spouses and/or Gold Star parents may be admitted on a space available basis. Determination of charges are based on the ability to pay; no veteran will be denied admission because of lack of income or excessive income.
